# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Secuura SEAT B KS-923 RE-GATE PASS WITH FINDINGS (#869, tier 2, narrow)** — `8b7d57cc6` (2026-09-06 21:44→21:55 AEST; five red-proof runs each printing its own SUBJECT + sha256, three DISTINCT subject hashes each matching what the tester computed independently BEFORE the run) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It converted the builder's INFERENCE into a measurement.** The post-API path was labelled inferred; the tester built a standalone probe varying only the mode of `06-tenant-isolation.sh` (reachable ONLY from that loop), with the precondition ASSERTED — it refuses to report unless `[ -r ]` is false and `ls -l` shows `----------`. Result: the fix covers it, and `require_job` at :129 is character-identical to the Stage-1 call at :105. It also closed the root caveat in both directions — ran as uid 501 with the cells discriminating, then checked the CI path (`pr-security-gates.yml:83`, `ubuntu-latest`, no `container:` key, so a non-root runner). **And it separated agreement from judgement:** it agrees the third fixture restates the same delegation, but observes the OBSERVABLE differs — the pre-fix post-API behaviour was rc 0, a gate PASS, while CELL 11 pins only a non-zero refusal. It wrote and ran that cell in under a minute, then deliberately did NOT file it or write it into the builder's tree. |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s141, seat A) | **KS-914 MERGED (PR #868)** — `a8aa723a0` → `ff5218867` (parents held, `babdbd4c2` contained, control fires — verified by Wednesday from objects) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **The delivered tree `6615878e` is byte-identical to the tree the gate re-derived** when develop moved under it mid-session. A merge receipt saying "no conflicts" is a claim about a process; a tree oid matching an independently computed prediction is a claim about the artefact. The live SSRF gap is closed on develop: after this PR there are exactly two service-side uses of `assertSafeOutboundUrl` and both are registration-time, so ZERO in-tree instances of the validate-then-fetch shape remain. |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s140d, seat B) | **KS-732 round 1 (PR #872)** — `a8aa723a0` → `235bb1ba3` (the MFA-disable endpoint demanded a password it never verified; built to Wednesday's three-part shape with all four conditions; auth suite 43 files / 595 tests / 0 failed) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **It corrected WEDNESDAY'S RULING before the code was built.** The ruling required "a valid `totpCode` or a valid backup code" for passwordless accounts — but `totpCode` is `.length(6).regex(/^\d+$/)` and backup codes are 8-char base32, so that branch could never have been reached; the agent had already written it and says it *"would have been dead code this very suite reported as covered"*. Caught by checking the field's constraint against the generator's output rather than trusting the design, and fixed by adding a SEPARATE optional field so Wednesday's own compatibility invariant still holds (`required` still `[password]`, 307 paths before and after), with a cell driving it so the branch is measured reachable. **Three tampers, each redding EXACTLY ONE cell with no collateral** — stronger than three reds, and the answer to the collateral problem it had itself named on KS-720. **Second spec finding, unasked:** the published description NARRATED the defect verbatim (written deliberately under KS-712 so the contract would not bless an absent check) — now false and replaced. Its framing: *a contract describing a defect is as wrong as one describing an absent check.* Its stubs default to FALSE rather than passthrough, so

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
